Correlational analysis of the relationship between attention and
choice in a 2-attribute binary choice task where attributes can be positive (P),
negative (N), or ambivalent (B). This repeats the PAS3 analysis on the PAS4
dataset.

Main Goals:

1. Characterize how attention is allocated across attributes and values.

2. Characterize how attention relates to choice, and whether this relationship flips
   for negative attributes.

3. Test whether choice sensitivity to value is range-normalized.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  cache = TRUE,
  autodep = TRUE,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5,
  dpi = 120
)
```

# Data Cleaning

Exclude subjects with corrupted attribute-type labels. In these subjects a subset
of trials have the P/N attribute labels swapped relative to their value signs
(e.g. an "N" attribute carrying positive values), so they are dropped before any
cleaning or analysis.

```{r exclude-subjects}
# Subjects flagged for swapped P/N labels on some trials (see data-quality check).
excluded_subjects <- c(420, 561, 679, 714, 967, 1015)

pas_raw  <- pas_raw  %>% filter(!(SubjectNumber %in% excluded_subjects))
long_raw <- long_raw %>% filter(!(SubjectNumber %in% excluded_subjects))
```

```{r clean-trial}
pas <- pas_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Subject = factor(SubjectNumber),
    WN  = factor(WN, levels = c("Narrow", "Wide")), # Narrow is the reference
    BPN = factor(BPN, levels = c("PN", "PB", "NB")),
    ChooseL = as.integer(ChooseL), # logical -> 0/1
    Correct = as.integer(Correct),
    Difficulty = abs(Diff),
    Diff_z = as.numeric(scale(Diff)), # scaled for brms sampling
    # Normalized net fixation: relative attention to left, 
    # free of total deliberation time (which is essentially RT). Guard against zero totals.
    total_dwell = DwellL + DwellR, 
    DwellDiff_norm = if_else(total_dwell > 0, DwellDiff / total_dwell, 0)
  )

# Refined trial type from realized B valence. The B attribute lives in whichever
# row is labelled "B". Identify its left and right values, then classify.
pas <- pas %>%
  mutate(
    B_left  = case_when(AttT == "B" ~ VLT, AttB == "B" ~ VLB, TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    B_right = case_when(AttT == "B" ~ VRT, AttB == "B" ~ VRB, TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    B_valence = case_when(
      is.na(B_left)            ~ "none",    # PN trials
      B_left > 0 & B_right > 0 ~ "pos",     # both B positive
      B_left < 0 & B_right < 0 ~ "neg",     # both B negative
      TRUE                     ~ "mixed"    # B switches sign across options
    ),
    BPN_refined = case_when(
      BPN == "PN"                      ~ "PN",
      BPN == "PB" & B_valence=="pos"   ~ "PB+",
      BPN == "PB" & B_valence=="neg"   ~ "PB-",
      BPN == "PB" & B_valence=="mixed" ~ "PBo",
      BPN == "NB" & B_valence=="pos"   ~ "NB+",
      BPN == "NB" & B_valence=="neg"   ~ "NB-",
      BPN == "NB" & B_valence=="mixed" ~ "NBo"
    ),
    mixedB = B_valence == "mixed"
  )

table(pas$BPN_refined, useNA = "ifany")
```

## Per-box long representation

Left boxes get a side sign of `+1` (looking there should move choice toward "left"); right boxes get `-1`.

```{r boxlong}
mk_box <- function(df, box, side_sign, type_col, val_col, dwell_col) {
  df %>%
    transmute(
      Subject, Trial, WN, BPN, ChooseL, Diff, Diff_z,
      box       = box,
      side_sign = side_sign,
      type      = .data[[type_col]],
      value     = .data[[val_col]],
      dwell     = .data[[dwell_col]]
    )
}

boxlong <- bind_rows(
  mk_box(pas, "LT",  1, "AttT", "VLT", "DwellLT"),
  mk_box(pas, "LB",  1, "AttB", "VLB", "DwellLB"),
  mk_box(pas, "RT", -1, "AttT", "VRT", "DwellRT"),
  mk_box(pas, "RB", -1, "AttB", "VRB", "DwellRB")
) %>%
  mutate(
    type = factor(type, levels = c("P", "N", "B")),
    # Signed dwell: positive seconds push choice toward this box's side.
    signed_dwell = side_sign * dwell,
    # Signed value: this box's value, signed by side. Scaled for brms sampling.
    signed_value = side_sign * value / 10,
    # Cell label for (type x value), e.g. "N_neg10", "P_pos5", "B_pos20".
    cell = paste0(type, "_", if_else(value < 0, "neg", "pos"), abs(value))
  )

glimpse(boxlong)
```

## Fixation-level cleaning

```{r clean-long}
long <- long_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Subject = factor(SubjectNumber),
    WN  = factor(WN,  levels = c("Narrow", "Wide")),
    BPN = factor(BPN, levels = c("PN", "PB", "NB")),
    fix_value = case_when(
      FixROI == "LT" ~ VLT, FixROI == "RT" ~ VRT,
      FixROI == "LB" ~ VLB, FixROI == "RB" ~ VRB
    ),
    fix_type = factor(
      if_else(FixROI %in% c("LT", "RT"), AttT, AttB),
      levels = c("P", "N", "B")
    )
  )
```

```{r fix-counts}
# Per-box fixation counts from the long file.
fix_counts <- long %>%
  count(Subject, Trial, FixROI, name = "n_fix") %>%
  mutate(Trial = as.numeric(Trial))

# Total fixations per trial (used as an exposure offset = attention share).
fix_total <- long %>%
  count(Subject, Trial, name = "n_trial") %>%
  mutate(Trial = as.numeric(Trial))

# Full 4-box grid per trial, with value and type, joined to counts.
box_grid <- boxlong %>%
  transmute(Subject, Trial, WN, BPN, FixROI = box, type, value) %>%
  left_join(fix_counts, by = c("Subject", "Trial", "FixROI")) %>%
  left_join(fix_total,  by = c("Subject", "Trial")) %>%
  mutate(
    n_fix = replace_na(n_fix, 0L),
    v     = value / 10          # scaled value for the linear term
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(n_trial), n_trial > 0)
```

# Basic Psychometrics

## Choice

```{r psy-choice, fig.height=4}
pdata_choice = pas %>%
  group_by(Subject, BPN, WN, Diff) %>%
  summarize(
    y_subject = mean(ChooseL),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(BPN, WN, Diff) %>%
  summarize(
    se = sd(y_subject) / sqrt(n()),
    y = mean(y_subject),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(pdata_choice, aes(x = Diff, y = y, color = WN)) +
  facet_grid(. ~ BPN) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  
  #geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 1), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(ymin = y - se, ymax = y + se),
    size = .1,
    position = position_dodge(width = 1),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  stat_smooth(
    method = "glm",
    method.args = list(family = "binomial"),
    se = FALSE,
    geom = "line",
    alpha = 0.7,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Value Difference (L - R)", 
    y = "Pr(Choose Left)",
    color = "Range",
    title = "psychometric curves, by trial type and range"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Fixation Propoerties

## Fixation duration by box and condition

```{r fix-prop, fig.height=4}
prop_dat <- pas %>%
  group_by(Subject, BPN, WN) %>%
  summarise(across(c(DwellLT, DwellLB, DwellRT, DwellRB), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(DwellLT, DwellLB, DwellRT, DwellRB),
               names_to = "box", values_to = "mean_dwell") %>%
  mutate(box = str_remove(box, "Dwell")) %>%
  group_by(BPN, WN, box) %>%
  summarise(se = sd(mean_dwell, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
            mean_dwell = mean(mean_dwell, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

pd <- position_dodge(0.9)

ggplot(prop_dat, aes(x = box, y = mean_dwell, fill = WN)) +
  facet_grid(. ~ BPN) +
  
  geom_col(position = pd) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = mean_dwell - se, ymax = mean_dwell + se), position = pd, width = 0.25) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = plt$wn_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Box",
    y = "Mean Dwell (s)",
    fill = "Range",
    title = "mean dwell per box by condition"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Fixation duration by value

Tests whether single-fixation duration tracks value. Expectation from prior work:
roughly flat. Durations are strictly positive and right-skewed, so we model them
on the log scale (a lognormal LMM); coefficients are interpreted on the log scale.
Fit with a subject random intercept; this chunk is the slowest of the
non-Bayesian models.

```{r dur-model}
dur_dat <- long %>%
  filter(FixDur > 0) %>%
  mutate(v = fix_value / 10)

dur_fit <- lmer(
  log(FixDur) ~ fix_type * v + (1 | Subject),
  data = dur_dat
)
summary(dur_fit)
```

```{r dur-plot, fig.height=4.5}
pdata_dur <- dur_dat %>%
  group_by(Subject, fix_type, fix_value) %>%
  summarise(y_subject = mean(FixDur), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(fix_type, fix_value) %>%
  summarise(
    se       = sd(y_subject) / sqrt(n()),
    mean_dur = mean(y_subject),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(pdata_dur, aes(x = fix_value, y = mean_dur, color = fix_type)) +
  geom_pointrange(
    aes(ymin = mean_dur - se, ymax = mean_dur + se),
    size = .1,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  stat_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE,
    geom = "line",
    alpha = 0.7,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = plt$type_colors) +
  labs(x = "Attribute Value", y = "Mean Fixation Duration (ms)", color = "Attribute Type",
       title = "fixation duration by attribute type and value") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Refixations by type and value

```{r count-model}
count_fit <- glmmTMB(
  n_fix ~ type * v + offset(log(n_trial)) + (1 | Subject),
  data = box_grid, family = nbinom2
)
summary(count_fit)
```

```{r count-plot, fig.height=4}
pdata_box_grid = box_grid %>%
```

# Option-Level Attention

## Net Fixation Bias

```{r option-level}
opt_fit <- glmmTMB(
  ChooseL ~ Diff_z * DwellDiff_norm + (1 + Diff_z | Subject),
  data = pas, family = binomial
)
summary(opt_fit)
```

---

# Attribute-Level Attention

We estimate a **signed attention weight**: the effect of
one second of dwell on a box, on the log-odds of choosing that box's option,
holding value difference constant.

A positive weight means attention is associated with choosing the attended option. 
A negative weight is associated with choosing against the attended option.

## Non-Parametric Test

Each (type × value) cell's attention weight is estimated with **partial pooling**:
every subject gets their own weight per cell, drawn from a population
distribution, and we report (and plot) the population mean. In a logistic model,
leaving these subject-level slopes out biases the population weight *toward zero*
(the marginal effect is attenuated relative to the subject-specific effect), so
partial pooling both de-attenuates the average weight and yields honest,
subject-aware uncertainty. The cell-level random slopes are left **uncorrelated**
(`||`) to keep the model identifiable and convergent; subject-level value
sensitivity (`SV_*`) keeps its correlated random slopes.

```{r flex-design}
# Attention design: signed dwell per (type x value) cell.
flex_design <- boxlong %>%
  group_by(Subject, Trial, cell) %>%
  summarise(sd = sum(signed_dwell), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = sd, values_fill = 0)

# Value design: signed value summed per type (SV_P, SV_N, SV_B). These three
# sum to Diff (the total value difference) but split it into attribute-type
# channels.
value_design <- boxlong %>%
  group_by(Subject, Trial, type) %>%
  summarise(SV = sum(signed_value), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = SV,
              names_prefix = "SV_", values_fill = 0)

flex_dat <- pas %>%
  select(Subject, Trial, ChooseL) %>%
  left_join(value_design, by = c("Subject", "Trial")) %>%
  left_join(flex_design,  by = c("Subject", "Trial"))

value_cols <- c("SV_P", "SV_N", "SV_B")
cell_cols <- setdiff(names(flex_dat),
                     c("Subject", "Trial", "ChooseL", value_cols))

# Population (fixed) cell weights are the plotted "average" attention weights.
# Each cell also gets an uncorrelated subject-level random slope (partial
# pooling) so the population weight is not attenuated toward zero by unmodeled
# between-subject heterogeneity. Value sensitivity (SV_*) keeps correlated
# random slopes.
flex_formula <- as.formula(paste(
  "ChooseL ~", paste(value_cols, collapse = " + "), "+",
  paste(cell_cols, collapse = " + "),
  "+ (0 + SV_P + SV_N + SV_B | Subject)",
  "+ (0 +", paste(cell_cols, collapse = " + "), "| Subject)"
))
flex_formula
```

```{r flex-fit}
# Weakly informative priors. Predictors are scaled (Diff) or in seconds (dwell);
# normal(0, 2.5) on slopes is mildly regularizing on the log-odds scale.
flex_priors <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 2.5), class = "b"),
  prior(normal(0, 2),   class = "Intercept")
)

# Heavier sampler settings for this hierarchical model: more iterations for
# stable tail-ESS on the random-effect SDs, and a higher adapt_delta /
# max_treedepth to suppress divergences from the funnel geometry.
flex_fit <- brm(
  flex_formula,
  data    = flex_dat,
  family  = bernoulli(),
  prior   = flex_priors,
  chains  = BRMS_CHAINS, iter = 4000, seed = BRMS_SEED,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12),
  file    = "brm_fits/PAS4_flex_attention_weights_typeval_partpool"
)
flex_fit
```

```{r flex-plot, fig.height=5}
# Tidy the cell weights into type/value for plotting.
flex_draws <- as_draws_df(flex_fit)

weight_summary <- map_dfr(cell_cols, function(cl) {
  x <- flex_draws[[paste0("b_", cl)]]
  h <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
  tibble(cell = cl, estimate = median(x), lo = h$CI_low, hi = h$CI_high)
}) %>%
  mutate(
    type  = str_extract(cell, "^[PNB]"),
    sign  = if_else(str_detect(cell, "_neg"), -1, 1),
    value = sign * as.numeric(str_extract(cell, "[0-9]+$")),
    type  = factor(type, levels = c("N", "B", "P"))
  )

ggplot(weight_summary, aes(x = value, y = estimate, color = type)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), size = .25, linewidth = 1) +
  #geom_line() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 1) +
  
  facet_wrap(~ type, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = plt$type_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Attribute Value", 
    y = "Attention Weight",
    title = "signed attention weights by attribute type and value"
  ) +
  guides(color = "none")
```

## Attention Weights by Range Condition

We repeat the partial-pooling attention-weight estimation **separately within
each range condition**, fitting one model on Narrow-condition trials and another
on Wide-condition trials. Narrow and Wide cover different attribute value ranges,
so each subset yields its own set of (type × value) cells. Plotting the two side
by side shows whether the mapping from attribute value to attention weight differs
between the narrow and wide ranges.

```{r flex-by-range-design}
# Build the same flex design as above, but restricted to a single range
# condition. Returns the per-trial design matrix for that subset.
build_flex_dat <- function(range_level) {
  bl <- boxlong %>% filter(WN == range_level)
  ps <- pas      %>% filter(WN == range_level)

  flex_design <- bl %>%
    group_by(Subject, Trial, cell) %>%
    summarise(sd = sum(signed_dwell), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = sd, values_fill = 0)

  value_design <- bl %>%
    group_by(Subject, Trial, type) %>%
    summarise(SV = sum(signed_value), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = SV,
                names_prefix = "SV_", values_fill = 0)

  ps %>%
    select(Subject, Trial, ChooseL) %>%
    left_join(value_design, by = c("Subject", "Trial")) %>%
    left_join(flex_design,  by = c("Subject", "Trial"))
}

# Build the flex formula for a given subset's columns (cells present can differ
# between Narrow and Wide).
build_flex_formula <- function(dat) {
  vcols <- intersect(c("SV_P", "SV_N", "SV_B"), names(dat))
  ccols <- setdiff(names(dat), c("Subject", "Trial", "ChooseL", vcols))
  as.formula(paste(
    "ChooseL ~", paste(vcols, collapse = " + "), "+",
    paste(ccols, collapse = " + "),
    "+ (0 +", paste(vcols, collapse = " + "), "| Subject)",
    "+ (0 +", paste(ccols, collapse = " + "), "| Subject)"
  ))
}

flex_dat_narrow <- build_flex_dat("Narrow")
flex_dat_wide   <- build_flex_dat("Wide")
```

```{r flex-by-range-fit}
flex_priors <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 2.5), class = "b"),
  prior(normal(0, 2),   class = "Intercept")
)

flex_fit_narrow <- brm(
  build_flex_formula(flex_dat_narrow),
  data    = flex_dat_narrow,
  family  = bernoulli(),
  prior   = flex_priors,
  chains  = BRMS_CHAINS, iter = 4000, seed = BRMS_SEED,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12),
  file    = "brm_fits/PAS4_flex_attention_weights_typeval_partpool_narrow"
)

flex_fit_wide <- brm(
  build_flex_formula(flex_dat_wide),
  data    = flex_dat_wide,
  family  = bernoulli(),
  prior   = flex_priors,
  chains  = BRMS_CHAINS, iter = 4000, seed = BRMS_SEED,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95, max_treedepth = 12),
  file    = "brm_fits/PAS4_flex_attention_weights_typeval_partpool_wide"
)
```

```{r flex-by-range-plot, fig.height=5, fig.width=12}
# Tidy a flex fit's population cell weights into a (type, value) summary.
summarise_flex_weights <- function(fit) {
  draws <- as_draws_df(fit)
  cells <- str_remove(grep("^b_[PNB]_", names(draws), value = TRUE), "^b_")
  map_dfr(cells, function(cl) {
    x <- draws[[paste0("b_", cl)]]
    h <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
    tibble(cell = cl, estimate = median(x), lo = h$CI_low, hi = h$CI_high)
  }) %>%
    mutate(
      type  = str_extract(cell, "^[PNB]"),
      sign  = if_else(str_detect(cell, "_neg"), -1, 1),
      value = sign * as.numeric(str_extract(cell, "[0-9]+$")),
      type  = factor(type, levels = c("N", "B", "P"))
    )
}

plot_flex_weights <- function(fit, title) {
  ggplot(summarise_flex_weights(fit),
         aes(x = value, y = estimate, color = type)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), size = .25, linewidth = 1) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~ type, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_color_manual(values = plt$type_colors) +
    labs(x = "Attribute Value", y = "Attention Weight", title = title) +
    guides(color = "none")
}

plot_flex_weights(flex_fit_narrow, "Narrow range") /
  plot_flex_weights(flex_fit_wide,   "Wide range")
```

---

# Range Sensitivity

This is a value-representation test, not an attention test. The question is whether
a given value difference moves choice more in the Narrow range than the Wide range.
We regress choice on the per-type signed value channels (`SV_P/SV_N/SV_B`) and
interact each with the range condition. Range normalization predicts the slope of
choice on value is steeper in Narrow, so each `SV_type:WNWide` interaction should be
negative (value drives choice less when the range is wide).

```{r value-design}
# Signed value summed per type (SV_P, SV_N, SV_B): how much each attribute type's
# value difference favors the left option. Built from value only -- no dwell time.
# (value_design was already constructed above; rebuilt here so this section is
# self-contained.)
value_design <- boxlong %>%
  group_by(Subject, Trial, type) %>%
  summarise(SV = sum(signed_value), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = SV,
              names_prefix = "SV_", values_fill = 0)

val_dat <- pas %>%
  select(Subject, Trial, ChooseL, WN) %>%
  left_join(value_design, by = c("Subject", "Trial"))
```

```{r value-fit}
# Population value sensitivity per type, interacted with range; subjects get
# heterogeneous value sensitivity via random slopes.
val_fit <- brm(
  ChooseL ~ (SV_P + SV_N + SV_B) * WN + (1 + SV_P + SV_N + SV_B | Subject),
  data    = val_dat, family = bernoulli(),
  prior   = c(prior(normal(0, 2.5), class = "b"),
              prior(normal(0, 2),   class = "Intercept")),
  chains  = BRMS_CHAINS, iter = BRMS_ITER, seed = BRMS_SEED,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
  file    = "brm_fits/PAS4_value_sensitivity_by_range"
)
val_fit
```

```{r value-readout}
vd <- as_draws_df(val_fit)

summ <- function(x) {
  h <- bayestestR::hdi(x, ci = 0.95)
  tibble(estimate = median(x), hdi_low = h$CI_low, hdi_high = h$CI_high,
         p_neg = mean(x < 0))
}

# Per-type: Narrow slope, Wide slope, and the Wide-minus-Narrow range effect.
# WN reference is Narrow, so b_SV_type is the Narrow slope and
# b_SV_type:WNWide is (Wide slope - Narrow slope).
slope_tbl <- map_dfr(c("N", "B", "P"), function(tt) {
  narrow <- vd[[paste0("b_SV_", tt)]]
  inter  <- vd[[paste0("b_SV_", tt, ":WNWide")]]
  wide   <- narrow + inter
  bind_rows(
    summ(narrow) %>% mutate(quantity = "1_slope_Narrow"),
    summ(wide)   %>% mutate(quantity = "2_slope_Wide"),
    summ(inter)  %>% mutate(quantity = "3_Wide_minus_Narrow")
  ) %>% mutate(type = tt)
}) %>%
  transmute(type = factor(type, levels = c("N", "B", "P")), quantity,
            estimate = round(estimate, 3),
            HDI = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", hdi_low, hdi_high),
            Pr_lt_0 = round(p_neg, 2)) %>%
  arrange(type, quantity)

slope_tbl
```

```{r value-readout-plot, fig.height=4.5}
# Narrow vs Wide value-sensitivity slope per type, with 95% HDI.
plot_dat <- slope_tbl %>%
  filter(quantity %in% c("1_slope_Narrow", "2_slope_Wide")) %>%
  mutate(WN = if_else(quantity == "1_slope_Narrow", "Narrow", "Wide"),
         lo = as.numeric(str_extract(HDI, "(?<=\\[)[-0-9.]+")),
         hi = as.numeric(str_extract(HDI, "(?<=, )[-0-9.]+")))

ggplot(plot_dat, aes(x = type, y = estimate, color = WN)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.4), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = plt$wn_colors) +
  labs(x = "Attribute Type", y = "Value-sensitivity slope (log-odds per value/10)",
       title = "value sensitivity by range condition", color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
